Messages.Author: Malcolm Sprye
Messages.Body:
Okay, so the matter of Caitiff being clanless came up at the NYC qualifier a couple of days ago. Someone was playing a weenie vote deck and tried to name caitiff for Con Boon. They found out that they couldn't do so. This re-raised some questions which I've never seen satisfactorily answered. Here they are:
1. Just to be clear, Caitiff is not a clan, correct?
2. Not all clanless vampires are Caitiff, correct? e.g. Shock troops is not caitiff.
3. I've seen discussions that involved reputable sources talking about a deck running Mukhtar Bey and third tradition to make caitiff babies ( I think they were for consumption by Al' Muntaquim). So, if caitiff isn't a clan, why does Third Tradition produce Caitiff babies, as opposed to generic, claness babies? The card says nothing about transferring nebulous keywords from the parent, just the clan.

So yah. I searched the rules, and all I found was a single mention which said that technically Caitiff are clanless. That's it.

Messages.Author: Adonai
Messages.Body:
1) Caitiff is a trait, not a clan.  LSJ 11-21-2005

2) Not all clanless vampires have the Caitiff trait.  LSJ 11-21-2005

3) New vampires sired by Caitiff are Caitff, by ruling. (Embrace, Third Tradition, etc.)  LSJ 12-28-2001 and  LSJ 01-02-2002

Messages.Author: Malcolm Sprye
Messages.Body:
OOF! I just thought of another complication caused by Caitiff being a communicable trait, as opposed to a clan:

If a Caitiff gains a clan somehow ( Revelation of the Sire, clan impersonation, derangement, etc), I assume they retain the "Caitiff" trait. I assume this, both because the cards say nothing about removing the Caitiff trait, and because many of those cards are removable, and thus the Caitiff will be a clanless caitiff if he burns them.

Further, any babies (s)he makes would then be Caitiff + X, for X = some clan. So you could, theoretically, end up with Al-Muntaquim eating clanned vampires. You could also end up with clanned vampires using revelation of the sire to change clans.  It's all very silly, but hey.

OOH! Vidal Jarbeux can start the madness by emulating the Caitiff trait while he makes a baby. You get to have a brood of Toreador Caitiff then.

Messages.Author: vtesocrates
Messages.Body: Revelation of the Sire removes the Caitiff trait. I expect those other cards do obscure the Caitiff trait while they are in effect.

Messages.Author: Malcolm Sprye
Messages.Body:
You are quite right about revelation.
Requires a ready non-sterile vampire who is not Caitiff. Put this card on a younger Caitiff. The vampire with this card is now considered to be a member of the same clan as the acting vampire. He or she is no longer considered Caitiff. His or her capacity increases by 1.

Given that Revelation specifically says it suppresses the Caitiff trait, I see no reason why the others would, any more than going anarch suppresses the Black Hand trait.

Messages.Author: vtesocrates
Messages.Body:
The answer seems to be that Caitiff is a bit like a clan and a bit like a trait. It's a trait that takes the place of a clan. It's not found on the same part of the card as other traits.

I'm just spitballing here. Basically as far as the game is concerned, Caitiff IS a clan except for any effect that actually looks at clan. In those cases Caitiff is not a clan.

None of those quotes address my confusion in any way. I understand that Caitiff is a trait that passes to babies. I also THINK I understand that things that affect clan DON't affect Caitiff. Therefore, I see no reason why, If a caitiff somehow gains a clan, they should not remain Caitiff. (this is based off the rules and rulings presented thus far)
IN FACT, the fact that Revelation of the Sire EXPLICITLY removes the Caitiff trait, would IMPLY that simply gaining a clan does NOT, inherently, remove the Caitiff trait. None of the ruling liked thus far address that question.
I grant that the answer to this question may be highly unlikely to affect any actual game... but I am determined to understand this (IMO needlessly complicated) issue to it's full extent.
